newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Saldanha seen taking 30 tankers a year.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Saldanha seen taking 30 tankers a year.

text.p: No more than 30 tankers a year are likely to visit the Strategic Fuel Fund's (SFF) Saldanha oil storage tanks when it was commercialised, acting general manager Howard Roberts said on Thursday.
This would be only four more than the number presently visiting the terminal and much less than the 75 originally envisaged, Roberts said in a statement.
SFF announced in 1996 that it planned to commercialise the underground tanks, which were built during the apartheid era to build up strategic stocks.

Since the first all-race election in 1994, the government has ordered that oil stocks be reduced to 36 million barrels from 48 million barrels. The tanks can hold 45 million barrels and the balance was stored in disused mine shafts inland.
The cutback in stocks left surplus storage space and Iran, which had supplied most of South Africa's oil during sanctions, was touted as the first customer.
But that deal was put on the backburner because of delays caused by environmentalists' demands that an environmental impact assessment study be undertaken before more tankers called at Saldanha.
"Prospects for an agreement (with Iran) remain poor as the parties have found it difficult to come to mutually acceptable commercial terms," Roberts said.
"Although SFF intends to pursue opportunities for storing oil in Saldanha for Iran or other parties, there is no concrete plan on the table at this stage."
Roberts said that the environmental study was expected to be released shortly and all interested parties would be invited to comment.
